profile.context: Lives in sheltered housing with a warden and attends with her niece; mildly hard of hearing.

facts.text: Burning when passing urine and needing to go much more often.
Passing urine about every hour in the day and getting up 3-4 times at night (usually once).
The stinging is about 5/10; uncomfortable but she is managing.
Urine looks cloudy and smells stronger; she has not seen any blood.
No fever, shivers, back or side pain, or vomiting; her niece has not noticed any new confusion.
Had a water infection about a year ago that was treated with antibiotics.
Takes alendronic acid 70 mg once a week for thin bones.
Uses a vaginal cream from the hospital twice a week; cannot remember its name (it is estriol cream).
Allergic to trimethoprim, which gave her an itchy rash.
Has stopped going to the residents' coffee morning in case she cannot reach a toilet in time.
Thinks it is another water infection and hopes to get antibiotics before the weekend.

contradiction.first_says: Oh, it's been about two weeks now.
